subject: Anthropology
title: Reproductive Technology
description: A micro-lesson that makes Reproductive Technology usable.

hook.text: A baby can now have five parents: egg donor, sperm donor, surrogate, and two legal parents. Kinship got complicated.

buildup.text: IVF, surrogacy, and genetic testing create new questions about who counts as a parent and what makes a family.

discovery.text: Different cultures answer differently. Some emphasize genetic ties; others value gestation, intent, or social care.

twist.text: Technology doesn't replace kinship rules. It forces societies to confront and redefine what parenthood really means.

climax.text: Reproductive technology shows that biology alone can't define family. Culture must decide what counts as kinship.

punchline.text: New technology, old questions: who is family?

quiz.question: How does reproductive technology affect kinship?
options: It makes kinship simple and clear
It forces societies to redefine parenthood and family
It has no effect on kinship

details.summary: Reproductive technologies like IVF, surrogacy, and sperm donation challenge traditional kinship categories by separating genetic, gestational, and social parenthood. These technologies force societies to redefine who counts as a parent and a relative.
details.whyItMatters: Reproductive technology reveals that kinship categories once considered natural are actually cultural constructs. When a child can have a genetic mother, a gestational mother, and a social mother, societies must decide which bonds constitute kinship.
takeaways: Reproductive technologies separate genetic, gestational, and social parenthood
They challenge traditional definitions of parent and kinship
Societies must create new legal and social frameworks in response

faq.question: How does surrogacy complicate kinship definitions?
faq.answer: A surrogate-born child may have up to five potential parents: egg donor, sperm donor, surrogate, and two intended parents. Legal systems struggle to assign parenthood when genetic, gestational, and social contributions come from different people. Each society resolves this differently.

faq.question: How do different cultures respond to reproductive technology?
faq.answer: Western societies tend to prioritize genetic connection in legal parenthood. Some Islamic scholars permit IVF only within marriage. Many indigenous societies focus on social parenthood regardless of genetic origin. Cultural values determine which biological facts matter legally.
